label: token right after an early "h h" / "e h" bigram in the original sequence
predicate: (phase == 0) & (prev_tok == tok("h")) & ((prev2_tok == tok("h")) | (prev2_tok == tok("e"))) & (t <= 4) & isin(in_tok, [tok(c) for c in "lkd3vuxf2rnj"])
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.02% of steps). It fires during the original-input phase on the token right after an h. 84% of activation mass has prev_tok == h, and almost all of it falls at t = 2..4 (never at t = 0, 1 or on the delimiter). Within that context the strongest activations, and most of the precision, come when the h itself follows h or e, so the input bigram is "h h" or "e h" near the start of the sequence (e.g. "3 h h [k]", "v e h h [k]"). Current inputs l, k, d, 3, v, u, x, f, r and n are favored over other tokens. The plain rule "prev_tok == h, early" has about 80% recall but only about 2% precision, so most post-h steps do not fire. The h/e condition and the in_tok list are the conditions that bring precision up. The in_tok list is a fitted lookup, not a clean category. Roughly 11% of mass is a weak, separate tail in the copy phase (mostly recall_idx 5-6, often outputting l), with activations around 0.5 of max. It does not fire on the delimiter, on the first two steps, or on later original positions much.
